stories.headline: US-Israeli Strikes Destroy Tehran's Century-Old Pasteur Institute on Day 35 of Iran War

key_facts.fact: US and Israeli forces struck Iran's Pasteur Institute, a century-old medical research center founded in 1920, rendering it unable to continue delivering health services according to the WHO.
key_facts.excerpt: US and Israel expanded their attacks on Iran, hitting a century-old medical research centre in Tehran, the Pasteur Institute; steel plants; and a bridge near the capital

key_facts.fact: WHO Director General Tedros said the Pasteur Institute played 'an important role in protecting and promoting population health, including in emergencies,' with two departments serving as WHO collaborating centres.
key_facts.excerpt: The institute played an important role in protecting and promoting population health, including in emergencies, according to WHO Director General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus

key_facts.fact: WHO has verified at least 20 attacks on Iran's healthcare system since March 1, causing nine deaths including frontline health and Red Crescent workers.
key_facts.excerpt: the WHO has verified at least 20 attacks on Iran's healthcare system since March 1, causing nine deaths, including frontline health and Red Crescent workers

key_facts.fact: At least 2,076 people have been killed and 26,500 wounded in Iran since the war began on February 28, with over 600 schools and education centers damaged.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 2,076 people killed in Iran since February 28. 26,500 wounded. Over 600 schools and education centers damaged.

key_facts.fact: A drone strike also hit a Red Crescent aid warehouse in Bushehr province on the same day.
key_facts.excerpt: A drone strike hit a Red Crescent aid warehouse in Bushehr province

key_facts.fact: US officials stated a bridge struck near Tehran was 'used to transport material for Iranian military drones,' though Iran contested this, claiming it was civilian infrastructure protected under international law.
key_facts.excerpt: US officials stated the bridge was used to transport material for Iranian military drones, though Iran contested this characterization, claiming it was civilian infrastructure

stories.headline: Iran Strikes Kuwait's Al-Ahmadi Refinery and UAE's Habshan Gas Plant in Escalating Gulf Campaign

key_facts.fact: Iranian drones struck Kuwait's Mina Al-Ahmadi refinery on April 3, igniting fires in multiple operational units, marking the third time the facility has been targeted since the war began.
key_facts.excerpt: Al-Ahmadi refinery fires caused in a number of operational units... third time the facility has been targeted since war began

key_facts.fact: A separate strike hit a Kuwaiti power and desalination plant before midday Friday, threatening water supply in a nation highly dependent on desalinated water.
key_facts.excerpt: Kuwait: Power and desalination plant hit midday Friday. Gulf nations are highly dependent on desalinated water.

key_facts.fact: Iran also struck the UAE's Habshan gas facility, the country's largest gas complex, which was shut down for the second time in 15 days.
key_facts.excerpt: Habshan Gas Plant (UAE): Iran's largest gas complex, shut down for the second time in 15 days

key_facts.fact: The UAE intercepted 19 ballistic missiles and 26 drones on the prior day, with 12 people injured from falling debris (7 Nepali, 5 Indian nationals).
key_facts.excerpt: UAE intercepted 19 ballistic missiles and 26 drones. 12 people injured from falling debris (7 Nepali, 5 Indian nationals)

key_facts.fact: The IRGC denied responsibility for the Kuwait desalination plant strike, instead blaming Israel for 'unconditional and illegitimate attack on Kuwait's water desalination centres.'
key_facts.excerpt: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps denied responsibility, instead blaming Israel for unconditional and illegitimate attack on Kuwait's water desalination centres

stories.headline: UK-Led 40-Nation Meeting Calls for Immediate Strait of Hormuz Reopening but Reaches No Agreement

key_facts.fact: Over 40 countries and international organizations including the IMO and EU attended a UK-hosted virtual meeting on April 3 to discuss reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: Over 40 countries meet to discuss ways to reopen the Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper convened the meeting, which called for 'the immediate and unconditional reopening of the Strait.'
key_facts.excerpt: Immediate reopening of Strait of Hormuz urged after 40-nation meeting

key_facts.fact: Participants discussed increasing diplomatic pressure and sanctions on Iran, releasing trapped ships and sailors, and rejecting Iran's attempts to impose tolls on vessels, but reached no concrete agreement.
key_facts.excerpt: they discussed putting more diplomatic pressure on Iran, including via the U.N., and rejecting any attempt by Iran to impose tolls on ships... but they didn't agree on anything concrete

key_facts.fact: France pushed back on calls to force open the Strait, with Macron trading barbs with Trump over the approach to the crisis.
key_facts.excerpt: France pushes back on calls to force reopening of Strait of Hormuz as Macron trades barbs with Trump

stories.headline: Russia, China, and France Triple Veto Blocks UN Resolution to Authorize Force to Reopen Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Russia, China, and France vetoed a UN Security Council resolution proposed by Bahrain and backed by Gulf states and Jordan that would have authorized 'defensive measures' to secure transit through the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia, China, and France blocked the Arab-backed resolution... Arab states sought a UN resolution authorising the use of force to ensure global freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: The three vetoing nations cited 'principled opposition to any language authorising force' as their reason for blocking the initiative.
key_facts.excerpt: The three vetoing nations cited principled opposition to any language authorising force as their reason for blocking the initiative

key_facts.fact: The veto effectively permits Iran to continue restricting oil and goods flow through the strategic waterway without international military intervention.
key_facts.excerpt: this blocking action effectively permits Iran to continue restricting oil and goods flow through the strategic waterway without international military intervention

key_facts.fact: The US and Israel continue military operations against Iran while rejecting ceasefire proposals, creating a contrast with the Security Council's inability to authorize collective action on shipping.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. and Israel continue military operations against Iran while rejecting ceasefire proposals—creating a stark contrast with the Security Council's inability to authorize collective action on the shipping crisis

stories.headline: Oil Crisis Morphs Into 'Everything Crisis' as Petrochemical Shortages Hit Medical Supplies and Food

key_facts.fact: The Strait of Hormuz closure has reduced global crude oil supply by approximately one-fifth, squeezing not just fuel but petrochemicals needed for everyday items.
key_facts.excerpt: The conflict in the Middle East has crimped oil and natural gas flows through the Strait of Hormuz, reducing global supply by about one-fifth

key_facts.fact: Plastic resin prices in Asia have risen up to 59% since late February, polyester chip prices jumped roughly 50%, and plastic bottle cap costs have quadrupled.
key_facts.excerpt: prices for plastic resins in Asia have risen as much as 59% to record highs since late February... Polyester chip prices: ~50% jump... Plastic bottle cap costs: Quadrupled since war began

key_facts.fact: The Middle East produces 17% of world naphtha, 30% of plastic resin, 45% of sulfur, 33% of helium, and 22% of urea/ammonia — all now in short supply.
key_facts.excerpt: Middle East production share: 17% of world naphtha, 30% of plastic resin, 45% of sulfur, 33% of helium, 22% of urea/ammonia

key_facts.fact: Japan faces fears that patients with chronic kidney failure won't get treatment due to shortages of plastic hemodialysis tubes; Malaysian glove manufacturers report latex shortages.
key_facts.excerpt: In Japan, the oil crisis has sparked fears that patients with chronic kidney failure won't be able to get treatment due to a lack of plastic medical tubes used in hemodialysis

key_facts.fact: J.P. Morgan analysts warned that supply constraints will intensify in April, saying 'the primary challenge has shifted from price to physical scarcity.'
key_facts.excerpt: The primary challenge has shifted from price to physical scarcity — J.P. Morgan analysts

stories.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth Fires Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George and Two Generals During Iran War

key_facts.fact: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth forced out Army Chief of Staff General Randy A. George, the 41st person to hold the post, along with Gen. David Hodne (head of Army Transformation and Training Command) and Maj. Gen. William Green Jr. (Army Chief of Chaplains).
key_facts.excerpt: Pete Hegseth has asked Army Chief of Staff General Randy A George to step down with immediate effect... Also fired: General David M. Hodne and Major General William Green Jr.

key_facts.fact: The New York Times reported the removal stemmed from clashes over Hegseth's decision to block promotions for four Army officers — two Black, two women — on a list of 29 personnel. George requested a meeting to discuss potential bias two weeks earlier, but Hegseth refused.
key_facts.excerpt: The New York Times reported the removal stemmed from clashes over Hegseth's decision to block promotions for four Army officers. Two blocked officers are Black; two are women. When George requested a meeting to discuss potential racial or gender bias two weeks prior, Hegseth refused to meet.

key_facts.fact: Christopher LaNeve, a former Hegseth military aide, is expected to serve as acting chief of staff.
key_facts.excerpt: Christopher LaNeve, a former Hegseth military aide, is expected to serve as acting chief of staff

key_facts.fact: Democratic Senator Chris Murphy said 'experienced generals are telling Hegseth his Iran war plans are unworkable, disastrous, and deadly.'
key_facts.excerpt: Democratic Senator Chris Murphy stated: experienced generals are telling Hegseth his Iran war plans are unworkable, disastrous, and deadly

stories.headline: Artemis II Crew Passes Halfway Point to Moon, Prepares for First Lunar Flyby Since 1972

key_facts.fact: The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen (CSA) — passed the halfway point to the Moon on Flight Day 3.
key_facts.excerpt: Mission is more than halfway to the Moon

key_facts.fact: This is the first time humans have departed Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972; the crew completed the translunar injection burn on Flight Day 2 to break free of Earth's orbit.
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time since Apollo 17 in 1972, humans have departed Earth orbit

key_facts.fact: Astronaut Christina Koch reported: 'We can see the Moon out of the docking hatch right now. It's a beautiful sight.'
key_facts.excerpt: We can see the Moon out of the docking hatch right now. It's a beautiful sight.

key_facts.fact: The crew is preparing the Orion spacecraft cabin for a lunar flyby planned for Monday, April 6, when they will photograph areas of the far side of the Moon never seen directly by humans.
key_facts.excerpt: Preparing Orion spacecraft cabin for lunar observation period on Monday, April 6

key_facts.fact: The first outbound trajectory correction burn was cancelled, indicating the spacecraft is on an accurate course toward the Moon.
key_facts.excerpt: First outbound trajectory correction burn was cancelled

stories.headline: ULA Atlas V Launches Record 29 Amazon Leo Satellites in Heaviest-Ever Atlas V Mission

key_facts.fact: ULA's Atlas V rocket launched 29 Amazon Leo internet satellites at 1:46 a.m. ET on April 4, the heaviest payload ever flown on an Atlas V.
key_facts.excerpt: Liftoff occurred at 1:46 a.m. ET on Saturday, April 4, 2026... the heaviest-ever payload for the Atlas V rocket

key_facts.fact: Previous four Amazon Leo missions carried 27 satellites each; detailed engineering work between ULA and Amazon increased the payload stack to 29 for LA-05.
key_facts.excerpt: The previous four missions for Amazon Leo launched on Atlas 5 rockets carried 27 satellites each, but ULA and Amazon Leo were able to increase the payload stack to 29

key_facts.fact: All 29 satellites were successfully deployed into their target low Earth orbit. The mission was delayed from March 29 due to high winds.
key_facts.excerpt: The Atlas V successfully deployed all 29 into their target orbit. The mission was originally scheduled for March 29 but was delayed

stories.headline: Utah Becomes First US State to Allow AI Chatbot to Renew Psychiatric Prescriptions Without a Doctor

key_facts.fact: Utah launched a 12-month pilot program allowing Legion Health's AI chatbot to renew prescriptions for 15 low-risk psychiatric medications including Prozac, Zoloft, Wellbutrin, and Lexapro.
key_facts.excerpt: Utah is the first state in the nation to test out a pilot program that will allow a chatbot to renew prescriptions... 15 medications considered to be low-risk including drugs like Prozac, Zoloft, Wellbutrin, and Lexapro

key_facts.fact: The program charges $19/month and excludes controlled substances like Adderall. Only 'stable' patients without recent medication changes or psychiatric hospitalization within the past year qualify.
key_facts.excerpt: $19 per month subscription... Patients will have to be considered stable, meaning they haven't had a recent change to medication or psychiatric hospitalization within the last year

key_facts.fact: The first 250 prescriptions will be monitored by a licensed physician, and the system must hit a 98% approval rate before operating without immediate oversight.
key_facts.excerpt: The first 250 prescriptions issued by the chatbot will be monitored by a licensed physician, and the system will have to hit a 98% approval rate before being able to issue prescriptions without immediate oversight

key_facts.fact: Utah's Commerce Department says up to 500,000 residents lack adequate access to behavioral healthcare, with most counties designated as having mental health provider shortages.
key_facts.excerpt: Most counties in Utah have designated mental health provider shortages, leaving up to 500,000 residents without adequate access to behavioral healthcare

key_facts.fact: Security researchers quickly demonstrated that the predecessor program (Doctronic) could be jailbroken to produce vaccine misinformation and dangerously alter dosages.
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers quickly demonstrated the predecessor program (Doctronic) could be jailbroken to produce vaccine misinformation and dangerously alter dosages

sources.title: Utah Is Giving Dr. AI the Power to Renew Drug Prescriptions
